slides.notes:
Welcome learners as they arrive.
Point to the title and read it: "Can I exchange this?" Say: "Tonight we return and exchange things at a store, and we change an appointment by phone."
Read the three lines under "Today you will". Give one quick example of each: "I'd like to return this, because it's too small." • "May I speak to the manager?" • "I'd like to reschedule my appointment."
Invented stores only (important): Valley Mart, its policy, and the eye center are invented. No play money is needed. Learners never talk about their own purchases, debts, or money problems.
Midterm next week: remind learners. The midterm reviews Lessons 1–7.

slides.title: Can I Exchange This?

runs.t: By the end of class, you can do these six things.
I can say I'd like to return this.
I can ask Could I / Can I / May I…?
I can ask for a refund or store credit.
I can change or cancel an appointment.
I can use I'd like and I'd like to.
I can read a return policy and fill out a form.

slides.notes:
Read each goal slowly. Learners repeat.
Goal 1: I'd like to return / exchange this, and a reason (because it's too small). Goal 2: ask for permission with Could I / Can I / May I…? and answer. Goal 3: ask for a refund or store credit, and ask for the manager politely.
Goal 4: change or cancel an appointment by phone. Goal 5: I'd like + a thing and I'd like to + a verb. Goal 6: read a store return policy and fill out a return form.
"We check at 7:25" = the Progress Check. It is not a test grade.
Lesson plan: At a glance: Objectives.

runs.t: The clerk reads the Store Policy Card.
30 days · receipt: refund · no receipt: store credit
Hi. I'd like to return these shoes.
The clerk follows the policy. Switch.

slides.notes:
Step 5 · 7:00–7:12 · Talk Time: Service Desk · 12 min. Pairs.
Round 1 (6 min): the clerk reads the Store Policy Card. The customer chooses a Customer Card and returns or exchanges the item. The clerk follows the policy. After each card, switch roles. Each click shows the next step.
Store Policy Card: returns within 30 days • with a receipt: a refund or an exchange • no receipt: store credit or an exchange • sale items: store credit only • more than 30 days: "Sorry, we can't take it." (The customer can ask for the manager.)
Model with one learner (1 min): you are the customer with card 1: "Hi. I'd like to return these shoes." → "What's wrong with them?" → "They're too big." → "Do you have the receipt?" → "Yes, here it is."
Customer Cards (answers): 1 shoes, too big, receipt, 10 days → refund or exchange • 2 lamp, broken, no receipt → store credit • 3 jacket on sale, stain → store credit only • 4 shirt, 45 days → sorry, more than 30 days (the customer can ask for the manager) • 5 coffee maker, wrong color, receipt, 5 days → refund or exchange • 6 pants, too long, no receipt → store credit or exchange. Wording will vary.
Invented stores only (important): Valley Mart, its policy, and the eye center are invented. No play money is needed. Learners never talk about their own purchases, debts, or money problems.
Lesson plan: Step 5; Talk Time: Service Desk; Answer key.

slides.notes:
Step 6 · 7:12–7:17 · Exit Ticket + Homework · 5 min · NEVER SKIP.
Exit ticket: each learner writes two sentences on a slip: one with I'd like to… and a reason with because (I'd like to exchange this shirt, because it has a stain.), and one polite question with Could I or May I. Collect at the door.
Homework: open the Homework page. Do item 1 together (one sentence on the board). Say: "About 15 minutes. Bring it next week. Next week is the midterm review."
Homework items: 1 what do you say at the service desk? Write I'd like to… and a reason with because • 2 write like or like to • 3 finish the phone call (the patient's words) • 4 review (Lesson 6): 2 sentences with If…, I'll….
Read & Write (7:17–7:25, on the Student Pages): the Valley Mart return policy; questions 1–5; then a return form. If behind: questions 1–5 only; the form becomes homework.

slides.title: Before You Go

runs.t: I can say I'd like to return / exchange this.
I can ask for permission with Could I / May I…?
I can change or cancel an appointment.
A. Listen to the teacher. Circle a or b.

slides.notes:
Progress Check · 7:25–7:30 · 5 min. Individuals. Open the Progress Check page.
Part A: read each sentence slowly, 2 times. Learners circle a or b. Then click to show the answer (one click per item, 1 to 4).
Say: 1 "I'd like to return these shoes. They're too big." (a) • 2 "Could I exchange this shirt for a large?" (b) • 3 "I'd like to cancel my appointment on Friday." (a) • 4 "Is Tuesday at ten available? I'd like to change my appointment." (b)
Parts B and C: learners do them alone. Walk around and help with the instructions only. B answers: 1 to return, 2 exchange, 3 too small, 4 a refund. C: answers will vary (for example I'd like to return this lamp, because it's broken. / May I speak to the manager, please?).
Part D: read each "I can…" line aloud and point to the 3 faces: 😀 "I can do it." 🙂 "With a little help." 😐 "Not yet."
Scoring: A /4 + B /4 + C /2 = /10. This is not a test grade. It shows who needs more help hearing requests (A) and with I'd like / I'd like to and polite questions (B, C).
Collect the pages (or check them at the start of Week 8). If behind: do the Progress Check at the start of the midterm review, while learners arrive.
Lesson plan: Progress Check step; Progress Check page; Answer key.
